As a Janitor, your core responsibilities will include: • Perform general cleaning duties throughout offices, breakrooms, restrooms, hallways, and common areas. • Sweep, mop, vacuum, and maintain floors. • Clean and sanitize surfaces, countertops, desks, and frequently touched areas. • Empty trash containers and properly dispose of waste. • Restock cleaning supplies, paper products, and restroom necessities. • Assist with general cleaning and housekeeping duties in warehouse areas as needed. • Maintain cleaning equipment and supplies in an organized manner. • Follow established cleaning procedures and workplace safety guidelines.
In addition, you will be expected to help maintain a clean, safe, and organized facility for employees and visitors.

job.description: Customer Service Representative Location: Grand Rapids, MI Shift: 1st Shift Pay: $24.00+ based on experience Job Summary The Customer Service Representative serves as the primary point of contact for business customers, ensuring a high level of service and support throughout the order lifecycle. This role is responsible for managing customer inquiries, processing orders, resolving issues, and coordinating with internal departments such as production, logistics, and sales to ensure timely delivery and customer satisfaction. Success in this position requires strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to build and maintain long-term customer relationships. What You'll Be Doing As a Customer Service Representative, your core responsibilities will include: Serve as the primary contact for customers regarding orders, product information, pricing, and service-related inquiries. Process customer orders accurately and monitor order status from entry through delivery. Communicate with production, logistics, and sales teams to coordinate order fulfillment and resolve customer concerns. Respond promptly to customer questions, requests, and complaints, providing effective solutions and follow-up. Maintain accurate customer records, order details, and communication logs within company systems. Provide customers with updates on order status, inventory availability, and shipment schedules. Investigate and resolve order discrepancies, shipping issues, and product-related concerns. Support continuous improvement efforts by collecting customer feedback and identifying opportunities to enhance service levels. Build and maintain strong relationships with customers to encourage long-term business partnerships. Assist with reporting, documentation, and administrative tasks related to customer account management. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High school diploma or GED required; associate degree in Business, Customer Service, Supply Chain, or a related field preferred. Previous experience in customer service, account management, order entry, or inside sales, preferably in a B2B manufacturing, distribution, or industrial environment. Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to interact professionally with customers and internal teams. Experience processing orders, managing customer accounts, and resolving customer concerns in a fast-paced environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Excel, and Word. Experience using ERP systems, CRM platforms, or order management software preferred. Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to prioritize multiple tasks and deadlines. High attention to detail and accuracy when entering orders, updating customer records, and reviewing documentation. Ability to analyze problems, identify solutions, and effectively resolve customer issues. Ability to work collaboratively with production, logistics, shipping, and sales teams. Strong follow-up skills and a commitment to providing exceptional customer service. Reliable attendance and the ability to maintain professionalism in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. job.title: 2nd shift -Process Technician Kalamazoo
job.description: Process Technician Location: Kalamazoo, MI Shift: 6 PM to 2 AM (Monday–Friday and some required Saturdays) Pay: $65,000- $85,000 Annually Job SummaryAre you someone who enjoys working with plastic thermoformed molding, being part of a team, and producing quality plastic Thermoformed products? We’re seeking a process Technician to join our team in Kalamazoo, MI. In this role, you’ll be a vital part of operations by helping efficiently produce high-quality Plastic thermoform molded products in a team-oriented environment. What You'll Be Doing Essential responsibilities include completing safe and efficient product changeovers; removing, installing, aligning, connecting, and verifying form tools, trim tools, stackers, rails, guards, cooling circuits, air lines, vacuum lines, and related machine components; purging and restoring tooling water or antifreeze systems as required; loading approved recipes and establishing startup conditions for heaters, oven zones, timing, forming pressure, vacuum, cooling, trim registration, stack count, and material conveyance; conducting first-piece and in-process inspections; identifying defects such as incomplete forming, webbing, thinning, warpage, poor definition, trim misalignment, contamination, short shots, stacking faults, and dimensional variation; adjusting one process variable at a time within authorized limits; documenting changes and results; escalating conditions that require engineering, maintenance, or quality support; completing startup, shutdown, line-clearance, and changeover documentation; maintaining accurate process sheets and machine history; supporting trials, validations, capability studies, root-cause investigations, and corrective actions; training operators on standard settings, defect recognition, process checks, and escalation requirements; and maintaining organized tooling, parts, work areas, and technical records. As a Process Technician, your core responsibilities will include:Assist in tooling assembly, disassembly and maintenance of tools and machinery. Remove and install form tool, trim tool, stacker and EOAT from machine. Set rail positions, trim positions, stacker positions and robot positions. Troubleshoot process issues with minimal to no assistance. Document process setting and process improvements. Perform full tool change from good part to good part. These are the base skills possessed by all Process Techs. In addition, you will also assist with setup, troubleshooting, and supporting other production tasks based on business needs.What We're Looking ForQualifications:Prior machine operator experience required Previous experience in an industrial or warehouse setting required Reliable attendance and strong work ethic Skills:Machine operation skills: Ability to operate converting machines to produce plastic mold injection products efficiently and accurately. Communication and teamwork: Strong collaboration skills to work effectively with co-workers and support production goals. Problem-solving abilities: Willingness to troubleshoot issues and learn from others in a fast-paced environment. Organizational skills: Ability to stay organized and meet production schedules. Commitment to safety and quality: Focused on maintaining company safety standards and producing quality work. Troubleshoot machine, mold, and material problems to reduce downtime and improve efficiency Accurately complete Process Verification and Tool Reports as required. Participate in die change activities and ensure proper care of all equipment. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and machine control systems. Why Join Us?This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. Must feel comfortable and confident inspecting each part, and if there is an issue, must communicate with supervisor. 9. Must have the ability to be very dependable with excellent attendance. Ability to work in a team based environment Dress Code: Long sleeves are recommended and short sleeve shirts are required. Full length pants are required (pants must not expose any skin). Steel toed work boots and socks must be worn at all times. Safety Glasses are required. job.title: 1st Shift - Quality Technician
job.description:
Quality Technician
Location: Three Rivers Shift: 1st shift Mon-Thursday 6am-4pm Pay: $20.00 per hour
Job Summary
Are you detail-oriented and committed to accuracy? We’re seeking a Quality Technician to join our team in Three Rivers, MI. In this role, you’ll play a key part in ensuring products meet quality standards before they reach customers. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys hands-on inspection work, follows procedures closely, and takes pride in maintaining high-quality results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
What You’ll Be Doing
As a Quality Technician, your core responsibilities will include:
? Inspecting products and materials: Perform visual, dimensional, and functional inspections to ensure compliance with customer and company specifications. ? Using measurement tools: Work with calipers, micrometers, gauges, and other inspection equipment to verify product accuracy. ? Documenting results: Record inspection findings, complete quality reports, and communicate issues to supervisors or production leads. ? Identifying defects: Detect nonconforming parts, tag or quarantine defective items, and assist with root-cause information when needed. ? Supporting production: Work closely with machine operators and assemblers to maintain consistent quality throughout the manufacturing process. ? Maintaining a clean and safe work area: Follow all safety procedures, handle materials properly, and support general housekeeping tasks.
In addition, you may assist with incoming material checks, final inspections, rework verification, and other quality-related tasks as needed.
What We’re Looking For
Qualifications:
? Previous experience in quality inspection, manufacturing, or assembly preferred but not required. ? Ability to read and understand basic work instructions, diagrams, or blueprints.
? Ability to use basic measurement tools (calipers, gauges, rulers, etc.). ? Quality Tools, PPAP, APQP, MSA, PFMEA ? Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
? Ability to stand for long periods and lift up to 40 lbs. ? ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System
? Dependable attendance and a strong work ethic.
? Willingness to work in a fast-paced, manufacturing environment.
Skills:
? Attention to Detail: Critical for identifying defects and ensuring product consistency.
? Communication: Ability to clearly report issues and collaborate with production teams. ? Problem-Solving: Helps identify quality concerns and support corrective actions.
? Basic Mechanical Aptitude: Useful for understanding how parts fit, function, and meet specifications.
Why Join Us?
This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth within quality, production, and manufacturing operations.

PAGE  1991 12 Mile NW, Sparta, MI 49345· (616) 887-1745 · (616) 887-8210 · www.lassondepappas.com 1991 12 Mile NW, Sparta, MI 49345· (616) 887-1745 · (616) 887-8210 · www.lassondepappas.com Job Description Job Title: Operator, Label Reports to: Manager, Production In the event this individual is not on-site the Manager, Production will be responsible for the Food Safety and Food Quality program. The Manager, Production will be responsible for food safety and food quality checks, in the event the Operator, Label is not on site. FLSA Status: Non-exemptLocation(s): Sparta, MichiganLast Updated: August 2023Direct Reports: N/A POSITION SUMMARY The Label Operator reports to the Production Manager and is based out of our Sparta Michigan location. This individual will be responsible for operating the labelers associated with the line the employee has been assigned to in an efficient manner. Employees must be able to work in a fast-paced environment with close attention to detail through many changes. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES (essential functions of the job) Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. Responsibilities include: Set up and operate a production machine in accordance with established procedures and guidelines Controls and adjusts machine settings to complete simple tasks accurately, according to specification, and in a timely fashion Knows the purpose and follows the proper operation of all safety switches, interlocks, and safety devices Performs label cuts properly Adjust the pick-up and lap-end glue for changing application needs. If adjustments are not effective, the operator will need to request maintenance assistance immediately. Must with maintenance personnel regarding labeler area issues to avoid downtime accumulation. Understands and can properly operate all machine controls Clean all labeler and labeler parts Adjust the label basket as needed Clear jams and re-time the machine Adjust the brushes to ensure proper label application Demonstrates proficiency in operating and adjusting the labeler Perform size/bottle changeovers Accountable for food safety, food quality, and regulatory requirements for their position Encouraged to notify management about actual or potential food safety issues Adopt and maintain all SQF requirements for their position Empowerment to work with supervision to resolve food safety and food quality issues within their scope of work Help relieve label inspector for breaks and lunch breaks, only if labeler efficiency and line feed are maintained Performs other related duties as required and assigned EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE Minimum Required Qualifications Six months experience in a manufacturing environment operating production equipment A high school diploma or equivalent Must have excellent verbal and written communication skills Must be detailed oriented and can multi-task Must have excellent time management skills Additional Preferred Qualifications Experience in the food/beverage industry a plus Previous experience in Manufacturing or production environment a plus Ability to direct, coach and train others. Consultative, influential, strategic thinking and problem-solving skills PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS This position requires sufficient physical ability to work in a production setting. FREQUENT: Ability to talk and hear; ability to stand, walk, climb stairs, stoop, bend and/or crouch; push/pull; lift up to 50 pounds; use of hands and fingers to operate machinery/equipment and all manual and electronic equipment in area of responsibility. Exposure to wet and humid conditions and fluctuations in ambient temperature (seasonal). OCCASIONAL: Squatting, kneeling, ability to reach above and at shoulder height. Ability to wear a dust mask, and perform Confined Entry using LOTO program. Exposure to toxic and corrosive chemicals. VISION: Ability to use close and distance vision, as well as color and peripheral vision with or without correction. Must be able to visually detect obstacles and potential dangers in a fast-paced production environment involving high speed equipment and powered industrial lift equipment. HEARING: Ability to hear in the normal audio range with or without correction. Exposure to noise levels from pumps, machinery, forklift traffic, bottle lines and exhaust fans. This job description is not intended to contain a comprehensive list of the responsibilities that are required to successfully perform in this position. Other duties as assigned are part of every job description. The conditions herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Equal Opportunity Employer Recycle Operator Location: Eaton Rapids, MI Shift: 1st Shift, Monday–Friday Pay: $17.51 per hour Job Summary Are you a dependable and safety-focused individual looking for a long-term opportunity in manufacturing? We’re seeking a Recycle Operator to join our team in Grand Rapids, MI. In this role, you’ll support the recycling and remelt operations within a fast-paced foundry environment, ensuring safe material handling, proper melt processes, and high-quality output. You’ll play a key role in maintaining production flow, reducing scrap, and supporting continuous improvement initiatives.
What You’ll Be Doing As a Recycle Operator, your core responsibilities will include: ? Maintaining a safe, clean, and organized work area to support zero-incident goals. ? Supporting daily recycling and remelt operations, including feeding grade-1 scrap into remelt furnaces. ? Monitoring oxide levels and melt quality to meet customer specifications. ? Tracking and reducing melt loss, dross, and scrap with a target of <7% melt loss. ? Ensuring equipment uptime and supporting the department goal of 90% utilization. ? Following process checklists to maintain quality and process stability. ? Working collaboratively with material handlers, quality technicians, and production leadership. ? Supporting cross-functional teamwork and backing up other positions as needed. ? Reporting any unsafe conditions or quality concerns immediately to a supervisor. ? Performing additional duties as assigned to support production goals. What We’re Looking For Qualifications: ? High school diploma or equivalent. ? Mechanical aptitude and ability to use basic hand tools. ? Ability to operate a lift truck and overhead crane (or willingness to learn). ? Strong attention to safety and quality. ? Dependable attendance and strong work ethic. ? Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing. ? Willingness to participate in training and continuous improvement activities. Skills: ? Safety Awareness: Essential for working around furnaces, molten materials, and heavy equipment. ? Mechanical Aptitude: Useful for understanding melt processes and equipment operation. ? Problem-Solving: Ability to identify issues and take appropriate action to maintain quality and safety.
Physical Requirements: ? Ability to stand, walk, climb, twist, bend, grasp, and lift up to 50 lbs. ? Ability to visually inspect materials and equipment. ? Ability to tolerate physical demands for up to 12 hours per day. ? Ability to hear instructions and communicate in a loud manufacturing environment.
Work Environment: ? Automotive manufacturing environment with exposure to industrial hazards, loud noises, and hot/humid conditions. ? Shop environment (75%): exposure to heat, noise, and standard industrial tools. ? Production environment (25%): exposure to extreme temperatures during summer and winter months. ? Shift work with overtime as required.
Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for individuals seeking long-term stability and growth in the foundry and recycling operations. We offer hands-on training, a supportive team environment, and opportunities to advance your skills. job.title: 3rd Shift - Receiving/Planning Assistant
job.description:
3rd Shift – Receiving/Planning Assistant Location: Warsaw, IN Shift: 3rd Shift – 10:00 PM–6:00 AM Monday–Friday; 6:30 AM if an off-the-clock lunch is taken Pay: $19.00 per hour + $1.25 shift premium Weekend Work: Rotating weekends after becoming familiar with the position Job Summary Are you dependable, detail-oriented, and someone who takes pride in doing accurate work? We're seeking a Receiving/Planning Assistant to join our team. In this entry-level role, you'll handle customer parts before and after heat treatment, build and break down production loads, complete required paperwork, and prepare finished parts for inspection or shipment. No heat treat experience is required. We will provide on-the-job training to the right candidate. What You’ll Be Doing As a Receiving/Planning Assistant, your core responsibilities will include: Load Building: Count, organize, and carefully build customer parts into heat treat loads while maintaining accuracy and part integrity. Customer Part Handling: Handle customer parts before and after heat treatment with care to prevent damage and maintain quality. Documentation & Traceability: Complete and sign required paperwork to maintain accurate records and ensure full traceability of customer parts. Load Breakdown: Break down completed heat treat loads and perform basic visual inspections of finished parts. Packaging: Package heat-treated parts for final inspection or shipment according to customer and company requirements. Quality & Decision Making: Make informed decisions during the load process to ensure customer requirements are met and quality standards are maintained. In addition, you will also be expected to follow all safety and company procedures while keeping your work area clean, organized, and efficient. What We’re Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: No previous heat treat experience required; training will be provided Strong attention to detail and accuracy Ability to count, organize, and accurately handle customer parts Ability to complete paperwork accurately Dependable attendance and strong work ethic Ability to make informed decisions and take responsibility for your work Willingness to learn and grow within the company Availability for overtime and rotating weekend work after becoming familiar with the position Skills: Attention to Detail: Able to carefully handle, count, organize, and document customer parts. Efficiency: Able to work efficiently while maintaining accuracy and quality. Decision Making: Comfortable making informed decisions and taking responsibility for the quality of completed work. Dependability: Consistently arrives on time, follows procedures, and completes assigned responsibilities. Accountability: Takes ownership of work and understands how individual performance affects customers and the overall operation. Teamwork: Works well with others and communicates effectively when issues or questions arise. What We’re Looking For in a Candidate The ideal candidate is dependable, accurate, responsible, and motivated to learn. You should take pride in your work and understand the importance of handling customer parts carefully and maintaining accurate documentation. This is an entry-level opportunity with room for growth. Individuals who demonstrate initiative, reliability, a strong work ethic, and the ability to learn may have opportunities to advance within the organization. Work Environment This is a controlled manufacturing environment supporting customers in industries including medical, orthopedic, aerospace, military, food handling, and stamping. The position involves handling customer parts, building and breaking down loads, packaging finished products, completing paperwork, and maintaining an organized work area. Employees must be comfortable working efficiently while following established safety and quality procedures. Job Title: General Labor

A Muskegon Company that offers complete metal part-making capabilities for a variety of industries; supplying laser-cut parts for low volume needs & stamped parts for high-volume programs with complete in-house tool making capabilities is looking for a qualified candidate to join their team. The candidate could be working as a Press Brake Operator; doing Metal Finishing; Inspection; duties as required. 

Key Outcomes:

  1. Machine Operation (press) 
  2. Lift parts as needed 
  3. Reposition work piece when making multiple or successive hits. 
  4. Grind and burn out sharp edges. 5. Inspect the parts.

  • Must have the ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, correspondence and memos; along with having the ability to write simple correspondence. 
  • Must have the ability to present information to one or more individuals. 
  • Must be able to interpret math problems, having the ability to add, subtract, multiply and divide units of measure. Will be required to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs. 
  • Must use common sense to carry out detailed written or oral instructions. 
  • Must have excellent problem solving skills. 
  • Must be comfortable and confident working alone as well as in a team environment. 
  • Must feel comfortable lifting between 10-50 pounds consistently throughout the shift; the required weight will depend on which job the candidate is working on each day. 
  • Must feel comfortable and confident inspecting each part, and if there is an issue, must communicate with supervisor. 
  • Must have the ability to be very dependable with excellent attendance. 

Qualifications & Skills Required:

GED or H.S. Diploma required 

Must have excellent communication skills 

Ability to work in a team based environment

Dress Code:

  • Long sleeves are recommended and short sleeve shirts are required. Full length pants are required (pants must not expose any skin). 
  • Steel toed work boots and socks must be worn at all times. 
  • Safety Glasses are required.

job.title: Truck Mechanic | 1st shift | $25+/hr
job.description:
Truck Mechanic
Location: Grandville, MI Shift: 1st Shift | Flexible Schedule Between 6:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Monday-Friday) Pay: Starting at $25/hr, based on experience Overtime: May be required as needed
Job Summary
Are you an experienced mechanic who enjoys working on a wide variety of vehicles and equipment? We're seeking a Truck Mechanic to join our team in Grandville, MI. In this role, you'll be responsible for diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining company fleet vehicles and equipment, helping keep operations running safely and efficiently. If you're self-motivated, mechanically skilled, and enjoy tackling different repair challenges every day, this could be an excellent opportunity for you.
What You'll Be Doing
As a Truck Mechanic, your core responsibilities will include:
? Diagnosing and repairing fleet vehicles: Perform maintenance and repairs on trailers, pickup trucks, forklifts, overhead cranes, and other company equipment.
? Troubleshooting mechanical issues: Identify and resolve mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and operational problems with minimal supervision.
? Performing preventative maintenance: Complete scheduled inspections and maintenance to maximize equipment reliability and reduce downtime.
? Reading technical documentation: Utilize prints, schematics, owner's manuals, and service documentation to facilitate repairs and maintenance activities.
? Maintaining repair records: Accurately document maintenance activities, repairs completed, parts used, and inspection findings. ? Supporting a diverse fleet: Work on a variety of company vehicles and equipment, as well as occasional personal vehicles owned by management. ? Ensuring workplace safety: Follow established safety procedures and maintain a clean and organized work environment.
What We're Looking For
Qualifications: ? Previous experience working on a variety of vehicles and industrial equipment. ? Ability to diagnose and repair mechanical issues independently. ? Experience performing preventative maintenance and general repairs. ? Willingness to work overtime when needed. ? Ability to lift up to 100 lbs. ? Strong work ethic and ability to work with minimal supervision. ? Comfortable working in a fast-paced industrial environment. Skills & Expertise: ? Mechanical Systems: Strong knowledge of vehicle and equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair. ? Electrical Systems: Thorough understanding of electrical systems and components used in vehicles and equipment. ? Hydraulic Systems: Experience diagnosing and repairing hydraulic systems and related equipment. ? Technical Documentation: Ability to read and interpret prints, schematics, owner's manuals, and service documentation. ? Welding & Fabrication: Welding experience preferred to assist with equipment and vehicle repairs.
? Preventative Maintenance: Ability to identify potential issues and perform routine maintenance to reduce breakdowns and improve equipment performance.
Work Environment
? Regular exposure to moving mechanical parts and industrial equipment.
? Noise levels in the work environment are typically loud.
? Physical duties may include lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling up to 100 lbs.
Why Join Us?
This position offers the opportunity to work on a diverse fleet of vehicles and equipment while utilizing a broad range of mechanical skills. You'll be part of a team that values reliability, problem-solving, and quality workmanship, with a flexible schedule that can be tailored to fit your needs.
Workbox Staffing Benefits:
• Weekly Pay • Hire-in Opportunities • Comprehensive Benefits including Health, Life, and Dental • Veteran-Friendly and Equal Opportunity Employer

job.title: Maintenance Technician | 2nd shift | $25+/hr
job.description:
Maintenance Technician
Location: Grandville, MI Shift: 2nd Shift | Flexible Schedule Between 2:00 PM - 12:00 AM (Monday-Friday) Pay: Starting at $25/hr, depending on experience Overtime: May be required as needed
Job Summary
Are you a skilled maintenance professional who enjoys troubleshooting, repairing, and improving industrial equipment? We're seeking a Maintenance Technician to join our team in Grandville, MI. In this hands-on role, you'll perform electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic maintenance on a variety of industrial machinery and equipment while helping ensure safe and efficient plant operations. If you're self- motivated, safety-focused, and thrive working independently, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.
What You'll Be Doing
As a Maintenance Technician, your core responsibilities will include:
? Troubleshooting and repairing equipment: Diagnose and repair electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems to minimize downtime.
? Installing and maintaining machinery: Dismantle, assemble, install, and maintain industrial equipment and production machinery.
? Performing electrical work: Troubleshoot and wire 120V, 220V, and 480V circuits, control panels, and related systems.
? Reading technical documentation: Interpret electrical prints, schematics, blueprints, and equipment manuals to facilitate repairs and preventative maintenance activities.
? Performing welding and fabrication: Complete MIG and stick welding repairs on steel up to 1" thick as needed. ? Moving and positioning equipment: Safely rig and move machinery weighing up to 20 tons using lift trucks, overhead cranes, and other rigging equipment. ? Supporting production teams: Assist machine operators in diagnosing equipment malfunctions and implementing corrective actions. ? Maintaining documentation: Accurately document repairs, inspections, and preventative maintenance activities to comply with OSHA, ISO, and company standards.
? Supporting facility maintenance: Assist with general facility upkeep, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, janitorial services, landscaping, trash removal, parking lot maintenance, and snow removal as needed. ? Promoting workplace safety: Follow company policies and actively support a safe work environment.
What We're Looking For
Qualifications:
? Previous industrial maintenance experience preferred. ? Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
? Strong work ethic and self-motivation. ? Ability to lift up to 100 lbs.
? Willingness to travel up to 20% as needed.
? Comfortable working in a diverse and inclusive team environment. ? Bilingual in English and Spanish preferred.
Skills & Expertise: ? Electrical Maintenance: Experience troubleshooting and repairing industrial electrical systems, including 120V, 220V, and 480V circuits. ? Mechanical Knowledge: Thorough understanding of mechanical systems, industrial machinery, gears, drives, and power transmission equipment.
? Hydraulic & Pneumatic Systems: Ability to diagnose and repair hydraulic and pneumatic components and controls.
? Rigging & Material Handling: Experience moving and positioning heavy equipment using cranes, forklifts, and rigging methods.
? Gear Systems: Working knowledge of large gears, helical gears, and worm drives.
? Welding & Fabrication: Skilled in MIG and stick welding techniques.
? Preventative Maintenance: Experience developing and completing preventative maintenance programs.
? Technical Documentation: Ability to read and interpret blueprints, electrical prints, schematics, and equipment manuals.
Why Join Us?
This opportunity offers a stable career with a company that values technical skills, safety, and continuous improvement. You'll work with a variety of industrial equipment, tackle new challenges daily, and play a critical role in keeping operations running efficiently.

• Weekly Pay • Hire-in Opportunities • Comprehensive Benefits including Health, Life, and Dental Insurance • Veteran-Friendly and Equal Opportunity Employer
Ready to take the next step in your maintenance career? Apply today and let's DO GOOD together!

job.description: Press OperatorLocation: Grand Ledge, MI Shift: 5:00 am – 3:30 PM Mon -Thu any OT will be on Friday.Pay: $17.27 Job SummaryWe’re looking for a reliable and detail-oriented Press Operator to join a busy molding and production team. In this role, you will operate presses, mix resin, prepare molds, inspect finished parts, and complete required documentation. The ideal candidate is safety-focused, mechanically inclined, and able to follow detailed production specifications. What You’ll Be DoingPour resin onto fiberglass sheets according to production specification sheets. Track production counts using counters and complete required paperwork. Clean molds using air hoses, apply mold wax, and prepare materials for production. Measure and mix resin and catalyst using dipsticks and air mixers. Operate presses safely and efficiently. Place fiberglass sheets into molds and verify part accuracy using fixtures and measurement tools. Work with robotics to verify water jet accuracy during first-part runs. Inspect parts for defects, perform minor repairs, and complete rework as needed. Adjust mold compression timing and temperature as instructed. Replace empty resin barrels and maintain clean buckets and molds. Conduct first-part runs, complete SPC charts, and obtain supervisor approval. Stamp parts with date and lot numbers. Clean resin run-out, gel coat, and machine beds. Record measurements on ratio logs and calculate mix ratios three times per shift. Report production numbers to supervisors. Troubleshoot production issues as part of a team. Review production boards to determine job numbers, lot numbers, and resin requirements. Spray adhesive and place tags as required. Complete Mix Ratio Logs and perform testing as needed per lab instructions. What We’re Looking ForQualifications:High school diploma or GED required. Ability to follow detailed work instructions and production specifications. Strong attention to detail and mechanical aptitude. Safety-focused and able to work in a fast-paced environment. Prior molding or finishing experience preferred but not required. Skills:Ability to operate presses and related molding equipment. Basic math and measurement skills. job.title: 2nd Shift- Lead Assembler
job.description: Lead Operator Location: Grand Rapids, MI Shift: 1st shift 6:00 am – 3:30 pm 2nd Shift 4:30 pm -2:00 am Pay: $20.00 //$ 22.00 per hour Job Summary The Lead Operator is the bridge between the production assembly track and the supervisory track. It is the first leadership tier on the floor. The Lead Operator performs hands-on production work as the primary part of the role while also leading their line, setting the example for quality and pace, helping others, and keeping the line running. The Lead Operator works without a supervisor present as needed, executing the work order on hand and resolving minor issues on their own line. This is a working leadership role, not a desk role. What You'll Be Doing As a Lead Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Production Perform hands-on production work as the primary part of the role. Lead the assigned line and set the standard for quality, safety, and pace. Cover absent operators on the line as needed. Perform routine equipment setup and changeover. Work without a supervisor present as needed, executing the work order on hand within the scope of the line. Directing and Assigning Assign tasks and workstations to employees on the line. Direct the work of the line, typically 5 to 12 employees. Execute the schedule and priorities set by the supervisor; escalate when changes are needed rather than redirecting independently. Problem Solving Resolve minor production problems on the line without escalation, with primary judgment over parts shortages and material handler coordination. Escalate quality stoppages and safety work stoppages immediately to the supervisor; the Lead Operators do not hold independent stop authority at this tier. Report employee conduct issues with the shift supervisor. People and Training Show others proper technique on the job (informal, on-the-line instruction). Serve as an operator a new hire can shadow, where in good standing. Provide verbal shift handoff to the Area Lead or Shift Lead. In addition, you will also be expected to monitor and maintain the output for the assigned line as well as maintaining a safe and organized workflow. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: Previous experience in production assembly lines of 2 or more years Experience in a team lead, supervisory, or manager role of 1 or more years Ability to lift, bend, twist, stoop, and maneuver 50 lbs. throughout a full 8-hour shift Skills: Expert knowledge of the products and processes on the assigned line. Sound independent judgment within the scope of the line. Clear verbal communication, up and across the line. Ownership of the line's output; reliable and present. Advanced assembly knowledge, tool proficiency, and the ability to troubleshoot common line issues. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth. The ideal candidate is an organized, analytical, and confident purchasing professional who can balance cost control with customer service and material availability. We're looking for someone who takes ownership of their responsibilities, communicates clearly, and can build productive relationships with vendors, warehouse personnel, sales teams, and company leadership. A successful candidate should be comfortable working independently, making purchasing decisions, negotiating with suppliers, analyzing data, and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Work Environment
The majority of this position is performed in an office environment, but the role will also require movement through warehouse areas and occasional travel to vendor locations or company branches.
The position may involve exposure to varying temperatures, humidity, cold, dust, and other warehouse conditions. The Purchasing Manager must be able to walk, stand, sit, stoop, perform overhead reaching, and lift up to 30 pounds as needed.
Ready to take ownership of purchasing, vendor relationships, and inventory management? Apply today and let's DO GOOD together!

job.title: 1st Shift - Furnace Operator
job.description: Furnace Operator Location: Detroit, MI Shift: 1st Shift Pay: $18.00/hr. Job Summary We're seeking a dependable and safety-focused Furnace Operator to join our manufacturing team. In this role, you'll be responsible for operating industrial furnaces used in the heat treatment of steel and aluminum components. You'll play a critical role in ensuring products meet quality standards while maintaining safe and efficient production processes. What You'll Be Doing As a Furnace Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Furnace Operation: Operate industrial furnaces used for annealing, hardening, tempering, solution treating, and other heat treatment processes while monitoring temperatures, cycles, and furnace atmospheres. Material Handling: Load and unload materials using forklifts, hoists, and manual handling methods while ensuring proper placement and securing of parts throughout the heat treatment process. Quality & Process Monitoring: Perform visual inspections and quality checks on finished components, maintain temperature logs and production records, and verify products meet customer and metallurgical specifications. In addition, you will assist with preparing parts for heat treatment, perform basic furnace maintenance and troubleshooting, report equipment concerns, and support production goals as assigned. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent required. Previous manufacturing experience required. Previous furnace operation or heat treatment experience preferred. Ability to read and interpret work orders, blueprints, and technical specifications. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and stand for extended periods. Forklift experience or certification is a plus. Skills: Attention to Detail: Ability to monitor furnace settings and maintain quality standards. Mechanical Aptitude: Comfortable working with industrial equipment and control systems. Quality Focus: Ability to inspect parts and identify potential quality concerns. Safety Awareness: Commitment to following all safety procedures and PPE requirements. Teamwork: Ability to communicate effectively and support production objectives. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth. job.description: Quality Inspector Location: Inkster, MI Shift: 1st Shift Pay: $17.00 per hour Job Summary We're seeking a detail-oriented Quality Inspector to join our team in Inkster, MI. In this role, you'll be responsible for inspecting finished steel racks and welded components to ensure they meet quality standards, customer specifications, and production requirements. This is a great opportunity for candidates with weld shop or metal fabrication experience who take pride in producing quality work. What You'll Be Doing As a Quality Inspector, your core responsibilities will include: Product Inspection: Inspect finished racks and welded assemblies for quality, dimensional accuracy, and workmanship to ensure products meet specifications. Quality Documentation: Record inspection results, communicate quality concerns to production personnel, and help maintain quality records throughout the manufacturing process. In addition, you will assist with identifying non-conforming products, support continuous improvement efforts, and work closely with production teams to maintain quality standards. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: Previous weld shop, fabrication, or manufacturing experience required. Ability to accurately read and use a tape measure. Ability to stand and walk throughout the shift. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds as needed. Prior quality inspection experience is a plus. Skills: Blueprint Reading: Ability to read and interpret blueprints is preferred. Weld Inspection Knowledge: Previous experience inspecting welds or fabricated products is helpful. Attention to Detail: Ability to identify defects, inconsistencies, and quality concerns. Communication Skills: Ability to communicate quality issues clearly with team members and supervisors. Reliability: Strong attendance and commitment to maintaining quality standards. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. job.description: Production Opportunities Location: Clare, MI Pay: $18.50/hr Shift: All Shifts Job Summary Are you a motivated and detail-oriented individual looking for a new opportunity? We're seeking a Production Operator to join our team in Clare, MI. Operating an Overhead Crane: Receiving and issuing raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas. Robotic Welding and CNC Machine Operation: Programming, setting up, operating, and adjusting process variables to meet quality demands. In addition, you will also be expected to maintain inventory control, complete entry of work orders and packing slips, and perform daily shift maintenance inspections. Not only will you be responsible for inspecting and managing raw materials and operating an overhead crane, but you’ll also be primarily focused on robotic welding and operating other CNC machines, including programming, setup, and adjustment to ensure quality products. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent desired. Two years of experience and/or educational related courses on related machinery desired. Experience/knowledge of blueprint reading, AutoCAD, CNC programming, thermal cutting machinery, and welding knowledge preferred. Ability to obtain a Crane License and fork truck license. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret the English language. Satisfactory math skills including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and basic geometry. Excellent problem-solving abilities. Ability to multi-task. Ability to operate machinery on a three-dimensional basis. Agility of the upper and lower body extremities, and capable of lifting 50 pounds regularly. Skills: Quality Inspection: To inspect incoming material for quality specification and quantities. Material Handling: To receive and issue raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas by operation of an overhead crane. Robotic Welding and CNC Operation: Primary focus would be working on the robotic welder and fabrication of products utilizing other CNC machines, including programming, machine setup, operation, and adjustment of process variables to meet quality demands. Inventory Control: To maintain inventory control by identifying and labeling raw material with proper identification. Computer System Entry: To complete entry of work orders, packing slips, etc., into the main computer system. Welding Knowledge: Must be knowledgeable in welding. Work Order Processing: To receive and issue raw material according to the work order, prints, routings, and bill of lading. Program Selection: To select appropriate programs utilizing the operating software, based upon the work order and print. Verification: Cross-checking that revision, part number, and description are correct. Before loading material into the machine, verify correct amount, size, gauge, and length of material has been loaded into the machine and issued to the work order. Measurement: Utilizing calipers, micrometers, and other measuring devices to verify accuracy. Quality Assurance: To check the quality of the first part for appearance and that the part meets print specifications. Assures that the fit, function, and appearance of products are at, or exceed quality standards. Production Fulfillment: Fulfills production requirements. Part Placement: To place finished parts in proper container/rack and designated location. Record Keeping: To record on work order all labor and downtime, documenting all information pertaining to each work order and routing. Maintenance: Performs daily shift maintenance inspection per the preventative maintenance (PM) checklist. Collaboration: Confers with the Team Leader or Crew Leader on any problems regarding safety, quality, production, inventory issues, etc. Confers with Engineering Programmer to maximize potential efficiency and quality gains in the manufacturing process. Work Area Maintenance: Maintain high quality standards as regards to machine and work area. Removal of all metal scrap, debris, and residue from machine as needed. Why Join Us? job.title: 1st Shift (Turn 2) - Production Associate (Eastern)
job.description:
GENERAL SAFETY TRAINING
WORKBOX STAFFING, LLC 1350 Scribner Avenue NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504 GENERAL SAFETY RULES 2 HAZARD COMMUNICATION – RIGHT TO KNOW 4 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES 10 BLOOD BORNE PATHOGENS 10 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE) 12 13 EYE PROTECTION 15 HEAD PROTECTION 16 FOOT PROTECTION 17 HEARING PROTECTION 18 HAND PROTECTION 19 MACHINE GUARDING 20 CONFINED SPACE 21 LOCK OUT TAG OUT 21 PREVENTING SLIPS AND FALLS 23 PROPER LIFTING TECHNIQUES
1 GENERAL SAFETY RULES
1. Report to work rested, alert and fit to give your full attention to the job. Of course alcohol and drug use is prohibited on the premises as is the residual results of use. Any employee discovered under the influence of alcohol or drugs will be terminated.
2. All work-related injuries must be reported to your supervisor and Workbox Staffing immediately.
3. Report any unsafe conditions to your supervisor and Workbox Staffing. NO EMPLOYEE IS EVER REQUIRED to perform work that he or she believes is unsafe, or that he or she thinks is likely to cause injury or a health risk to themselves or others. Contact WorkBox immediately if you have any safety concerns your worksite supervisor cannot address.
4. Horseplay, ‘practical jokes,’ etc., are forbidden. Employees are required to work in an injury-free manner displaying accepted levels of behavior. Conduct that places the employee or others at risk, or which threatens or intimidates others, is forbidden.
5. You are responsible to keep your work area clean and safe. Maintain a general condition of good housekeeping in all work areas at all times.
6. Learn where fire extinguishers and first aid kits are located at each assignment.
7. At the time of your work assignment you will be instructed on wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) if it is required for the assignment: Inspect PPE prior to each use. Do not use damaged PPE. You are required to maintain and keep PPE clean. Not wearing required PPE is cause for disciplinary action up to and including termination.
8. You must specifically be authorized by WorkBox and trained by your supervisor to operate the following equipment INCLUDING, but not limited to: Forklifts, Machines, Power Tools, Welders, and Cranes/ Hoist while on assignment. Contact WorkBox immediately if you are asked to do
9. When operating machines: do not wear loose clothing, ensure that long hair is tied- back, remove jewelry, and keep long sleeves either rolled up or pulled all the way down.
10. Never operate damaged or defective equipment. Turn the machine off and report it to your supervisor immediately.
11. Never tamper with, remove, or deactivate machine guards or controls designed to ensure safe operation. Never operate machinery without guards in place.
2 12. Never reach into a machine to clear a jam, clean inside the machine or for any other reason unless it has been properly locked out at the power source(s).
13. Do not remove any lock or tag from machinery. 14. Use proper lifting techniques and if an item is too heavy or awkward to lift, look for
an alternative method and/or have another employee help you lift the item. 15. Learn safe work practices. When in doubt about performing a task safely, contact
your supervisor for instructions and training. 16. Always perform your assigned tasks in a safe and proper manner; do not take
shortcuts. The taking of shortcuts and the ignoring of established safety rules is a leading cause of employee injury.
3 HAZARD COMMUNICATION – RIGHT TO KNOW
If your assignment or work site has or uses any hazardous chemicals you will get specific training on the handling, personal protective equipment required, and use of these chemicals at your job site. This training is a basic introduction to OSHA requirements.
PURPOSE OF OSHA’S HAZARD COMMUNICATION STANDARD
To ensure that employers and employees know about work hazards and how to protect themselves so that the incidence of illnesses and injuries due to hazardous chemicals is reduced.
EMPLOYER RESPONSIBILITIES
• Identify and list hazardous chemicals in their workplaces • Obtain Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) and labels for each hazardous chemical, if not
provided by the manufacturer, importer, or distributor • Implement a written HazCom program, including labels, SDSs, and employee
training • Communicate hazard information to employees through labels, SDSs, and formal
training programs
WRITTEN HAZCOM PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS
• Describes container labeling, SDSs, and employee training for each workplace • List of the hazardous chemicals • Make information regarding hazards and protective measures available to other
employers onsite
HOW MUST CHEMICALS BE LABELED?
Each container of hazardous chemicals entering the workplace must be labeled or marked with:
• Identity of the chemical • Appropriate hazard warnings • Name and address of the responsible party
4 SAMPLES OF LABELING AND HOW TO READ LABELS
Chemical Name 0 = minimal hazard 1 = slight hazard
HEALTH 0 2 = moderate hazard FLAMMABILITY 3 = serious hazard
0 4 = severe hazard
PHYSICAL HAZARD 0
PERSONAL PROTECTION 0 SPECIAL HAZARD
The Blue Section – Health Risks
4 The substance is a severe health risk if the substance is not handled safely. Substances carrying a four in the blue section could cause
death or irreversible injury.
3 The substance could cause serious temporary or irreversible injury. 2 The substance could cause temporary incapacitation. 1 The substance could cause irritation. 0 There is no health hazard.
5 The Red Section – Fire Risks
4 A flammable vapor or gas, which burns readily. 3 A flammable liquid or solid, which can be readily ignited. 2 The substance must be heated for ignition. 1 The substance must be preheated before ignition can occur. 0 There is no fire hazard.
The Yellow Section – Reactivity Hazard
4 The substance is readily capable of detonation or explosive reaction. 3 The substance may detonate when exposed to heat or an ignition
source.
2 The substance is readily capable of non-explosive reaction. 1 The substance may become unstable at high temperatures. 0 The substance is stable.
The White Section – Special Hazards
OX Oxidizer ACID Acid ALK Alkali COR Corrosive
W Use no water
Radioactive
6 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT
7 Safety Data Sheets (SDS)
The location of SDS Sheets is noted on your employee assignment sheet and/or communicated to by your site supervisor at the start of your assignment. These sheets are prepared by the chemical manufacturer or importer and describe:
• Physical hazards, such as fire and explosion • Health hazards, such as signs of exposure • Routes of exposure • Precautions for safe handling and use • Emergency and first-aid procedures • Control measures • Must be in English and include information regarding the specific chemical identity
and common names • Must provide information about the:
• Physical and chemical characteristics • Health effects • Exposure limits • Carcinogenicity (cancer-causing) • Identification (name, address, and telephone number) of the organization
responsible for preparing the sheet • Must be readily accessible to employees in their work area
EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITY - SAFETY HANDLING OF CHEMICALS
a) Do not handle chemicals that you are not trained to handle.
b) A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) must be secured for all chemicals purchased or brought on site. You have a right to access SDSs – ask your supervisor.
c) Follow all label and SDS instructions – including amount instructions
d) Do not mix chemicals unless authorized to do so.
e) Keep all chemicals in closed containers.
8 f) Store all flammable liquids in safety cabinets or safety cans. Never use flammable chemicals around ignition sources such as smokers, pilot lights, or arcing/sparking electrical equipment.
g) Wear required Personal Protective Equipment and minimize contact with the chemical.
h) Do not eat, drink, or smoke while using chemicals. And always wash your hands after handling chemicals.
i) Do not attempt to clean up a hazardous substance unless you are properly trained and authorized.
9 EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
1. In the event of any serious injury or fire, call 911 unless specifically directed or trained by your site supervisor to use a different number or protocol. Send someone to the facility entrance to meet the Fire Department. If in doubt, call 911.
2. Should you discover a fire while on assignment, alert others in immediate danger and initiate facility-wide fire alarm.
3. When an evacuation signal is given for any reason, all employees should immediately turn off equipment, close doors, and evacuate to their designated evacuation areas. Attendance should be taken to account for all personnel. Stay together in the group until further instructions are received.
4. WorkBox does not expect their employees to fight fires at the workplace. Your first priority is your safety and the safety of others. Under no circumstances should you attempt to fight any fire which is larger than a waste basket, too hot, too smoky, or if you are concerned for your safety.
5. If you choose to use a fire extinguisher, remember PASS:
• P = Pull (the safety pin) • A = Aim (at the base of the fire) • S = Squeeze (the lever) • S = Sweep (side to side)
If you use a fire extinguisher, remember:
• Stay low, • Keep yourself between the fire and an exit, • Do not turn your back on a fire, and • Immediately report the use of the extinguisher to your site supervisor and
to your WorkBox supervisor..
BLOOD BORNE PATHOGENS
The term ‘universal precautions’ means that you should assume that blood or other bodily fluids contain bloodborne pathogens that can cause disease and to protect yourself accordingly. Do not touch another person’s blood or any other bodily fluid during or following an incident. If you are trained to administer first aid, use gloves and other barriers that should be located with the first aid equipment. Always use protective personal equipment such as gloves if cleaning up blood or other bodily fluid and use a diluted bleach solution or other sanitizing agent. Dispose of PPE and cleaning towels in a secure way that won’t potentially infect others. If you think that you have been exposed to bodily fluid, notify your site supervisor and your WorkBox supervisor immediately.
10 11 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
PPE includes all equipment designed to provide protection to the wearer from potential hazards to the eyes, face hands, head, feet, ears, and extremities.
Eye/Face Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the face and eyes during exposure to such hazards as: flying particles, molten metal or sparks, liquid chemicals, acids or caustic liquids, or potentially injurious light radiation (i.e., lasers, welding etc.)
Foot Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the feet and toes during exposure to situations with the potential for foot injuries such as: falling or rolling objects, chemical or liquid exposures, piercing objects through the sole or uppers, and/or where the employee’s feet are exposed to electrical hazards.
Hand Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the hands during exposures to potential hazards such as sharp objects, abrasive surfaces, temperature extremes, and chemical contact. Hand protection is selected based upon the hazards and performance characteristics of the gloves.
Head Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the head during exposures to potential hazards such as falling objects, striking against low hanging objects, or electrical hazards.
Hearing Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to an individual’s hearing during exposure to high noise levels.
Respiratory Protection – Equipment designed to provide protection to the wearer from potential inhalation hazards such as: vapors, mist, particulates, and gases.
EMPLOYEE RESPONSIBILITY
1. The employee assignment sheet outlines the basic safety equipment that is required to be worn when on assignment.
2. Additional PPE may be required when performing certain tasks. Your site supervisor is responsible for training you and showing you the proper use and wear of PPE.
3. You are expected to attend the required training.
4. You are also responsible for caring for, cleaning, storing and maintaining PPE as required.
5. Inform your site supervisor immediately of the need to repair or replace PPE. Also inform your WorkBox supervisor.
12 EYE PROTECTION
What are some of the causes of eye injuries?
• Dust and other flying particles, such as metal shavings or sawdust • Molten metal that might splash • Acids and other caustic liquid chemicals that might splash • Blood and other potentially infectious body fluids that might splash, spray, or splatter • Intense light such as those created by welding and lasers
Safety Glasses
• Used for moderate impact from particles produced from jobs such as: carpentry, woodworking, grinding, and machine operation.
• Requires side shields. • Prescription glasses are not safety glasses. You are required
to have other prescription safety glasses.
Goggles
• Used to protect eyes, eye sockets, and the facial area immediately by surrounding the eyes from impact, dust, and splashes.
• Some goggles fit over corrective lenses.
13 EYE PROTECTION (CONTINUED)
Welding Shield
• Protects eyes and burns caused by infrared or intense radiant light.
• Protects face and eyes from flying sparks, metal splatter, and slag chips produced during welding, brazing, soldering, and torch cutting.
Laser Safety Goggles
• Protects your eyes from intense concentration of light produced by lasers.
• Used in conjunction with curtains.
Face Shields
• Protects the face from nuisance dust and potential splashes or sprays of hazardous liquids.
• Does not protect employees from impact hazards. • Safety glasses should be worn underneath shield.
14 HEAD PROTECTION
What are some of the causes of head injuries? • Falling objects • Bumping head against fixed objects, such as exposed pipes or beams • Contact with exposed electrical conductors
Classes of Hard Hats
Class G (formerly Class A) • General service (e.g., mining, building construction, shipbuilding, and manufacturing) • Good impact protection but limited voltage protection
Class E (formerly Class B) • Electrical work • Protect against falling objects, high-voltage shock/burns
Class C • Designed for comfort, offers limited protection • Protects heads that may bump against fixed objects, but does not protect against falling objects or electrical shock
Hard Hats
• Hard hats offer more protection than bump caps. They have an outer shell that is hard and durable to deflect potential head blows. Inside, hard harts have a lining that is shock absorbing. Also, some hard hats can provide protection from electrical shocks.
Bump Hats
• Bump caps are more lightweight than hard hats, making them more comfortable and proving to be less stressful on your neck, head, and back.
• They are ideal in situations where it is not required to wear a hard hat, but injury could still occur. They are often used in warehouses and food processing plants.
15 FOOT PROTECTION
What are some causes of foot injuries?
• Heavy objects such as barrels or tools that might roll onto or fall on the employee’s feet • Sharp objects such as nails or spikes that might pierce the soles or uppers of ordinary
shoes • Molten metal that might splash on feet • Hot or wet surfaces • Slippery surfaces
Steel Toe Shoes/Boots • Safety shoes/boots that have steel reinforced toes in case
something fall on your feet.
• Commonly required by some employers and readily
available at most shoe stores.
Metatarsal Boots and Covers
• Protects the upper foot (metatarsal bones) and toe area from hazards. A work boot with a built-in metatarsal guard will protect your upper foot and toe area from heavy falling objects- especially important for a workspace with heavy equipment, machinery, and containers.
Rubber Sole/Non-slip/Closed Toe Footwear
• You are required to wear rubber sole/non-slip/closed toe footwear on all assignments.
Rubber Boots
• To be used when working in slippery/wet conditions and while using chemicals.
16 HEARING PROTECTION
When do you need hearing protections?
• Noise can damage your hearing permanently whether at work, home, or during leisure activities.
• If the noise is 85 decibels or more, you are required to use ear protection. • A general way to measure this is if you have to raise your voice to talk to the people
standing next to you.
Earplugs
• Reduces noise levels to protect hearing. • These are convenient and disposable.
Earmuffs
• Easy to use and comfortable to wear. • Reduces noise levels to protect hearing.
Canal Caps
• Easy to use and comfortable to wear. • Reduces noise levels to protect hearing. • Hearing protection on a band that can be worn under
the chin, over the head, or behind the neck. • These can be put on and taken off easily.
17 HAND PROTECTION
Common Hand Injuries you need to guard against
• Burns • Bruises • Abrasions • Cuts • Punctures • Fractures • Amputations • Chemical Exposure
Metal Mesh Gloves or Kevlar Gloves
These gloves are used to protect hands from accidental cuts and scratches. They are most commonly used by persons working with cutting tools or other sharp objects and materials.
Fabric/Canvas Gloves
Made of cotton or fabric blends and are generally used to improve grip when handling slippery objects. They also help insulate hands from mild heat or cold. These gloves do not provide a lot of protection against cuts or lacerations.
Leather Gloves
These gloves are used to guard against injuries from sparks or scraping against rough surfaces. They are also used in combination with an insulated liner when working with electricity.
Aluminized Gloves
Gloves made of aluminized fabric are designed to insulate hands from intense heat. These gloves are most commonly when working with molten materials.
Chemical Resistant Gloves
These gloves are made of rubber, neoprene, polyvinyl alcohol, or vinyl. The gloves protect from corrosives, oils, and solvents. You should consult your supervisor for the proper hand protection.
18 MACHINE GUARDING
The machines you work with can contain moving parts with many hazards. Best safety practices involve the use of engineering controls and safe work procedures designed and developed to protect you when working with machines. This includes the use of machine guards. Machine guards safely contain and create a barrier of protection against the dangers.
• Know the potential hazards associated with the machines you use • Understand the role of machine guards and their function • Follow safe work practices when working with machines • Inspect the machine guards on a regular basis • Report any missing or malfunctioning guard immediately
NEVER REMOVE GUARDS
As a machine operator, you are directly affected by machine related hazards. Personal protective equipment, engineering controls, and safe work practices are all important parts of a safe working environment. Machine guards are only one part of this formula.
It is your responsibility to never remove or override these safeguards. A guard that is overridden or disregarded is the same as no guard at all.
EXPOSURE TO ENERGIZED PARTS
Contact with energized parts can cause electrical shock. The severity of the shock is determined by: the nominal voltage, the length of contact, the route of electricity through the body.
EXPOSURE TO MOVING PARTS
Nip points, pinch points, shear points and snag points are the cause of many finger and hand injuries including amputation when not properly respected. Motions such as rotating, reciprocating and transversing, become hazardous when clothing, jewelry or skin contact moving parts. Conveyor belts, gears and couplings are all examples of machine parts with hazardous motions. Actions occur at the point of operation and usually involve one of the three types of motions described earlier. Actions include: Cutting, Punching, Shearing, and Bending.
PROJECTILES
Projectiles from scrap material and foreign objects such as dropped tools can cause injury when working with machines. If an area with parts moving at high speeds is not properly guarded, a tool or item dropped or knocked into this area can become a dangerous projectile.
19 MACHINE GUARDING (Continued)
CATEGORIES OF GUARDS There are a great number of different types of machine guards found in the work environment. All types of machine guards fall into one of three categories: Barrier guards, Distance guards and Physical guards. Fixed
A fixed guard is a permanent fixture of the machine and does not depend on moving parts to function. It is generally constructed of sheet metal, screen, wire cloth, bars, plastic, or any other material that can withstand impacts and prolonged use.
Interlocked
When an interlocked guard is opened or removed, the tripping mechanism and/or power automatically shuts off, effectively stopping all moving parts. This prevents the machine from cycling or starting until the guard is back in place. An interlocked guard uses electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, or pneumatic power or any combination of these.
Adjustable
Adjustable guards provide a barrier that can be adjusted for various production operations.
Self-adjusting
A self-adjusting guard automatically adjusts for the size of the stock. Once the stock is removed, the guard returns to its normal resting position. It may be constructed of plastic, metal, or any other substantial material.
CONFINED SPACE
WorkBox does not allow temporary employees in permit-required confined space. If you believe that your job requires permit-required confined space entry, contact your WorkBox supervisor prior to undertaking the work. (Permit-required confined spaces are areas not meant for human occupancy, have limited means of entry/exit, and have electrical, chemical, thermal, atmosphere, or entrapment hazards).
20 LOCK OUT TAG OUT
Prior to working on any machinery when guards are removed, every energy source (electrical, hydraulic, chemical, mechanical, etc.) must be deactivated, stored energy dissipated, and the control (for example, the circuit breaker) padlocked so the machine cannot be started without removing the lock.
Never remove or tamper with a lockout performed by another employee or contractor. A lockout consists of a lock applied to a control such as a switch, breaker, or valve. A tag containing words such as “DANGER - DO NOT OPERATE” may also be used if the machine cannot be locked out for some reason (‘tagout’). If you see the lock, the tag, or both applied to an energy control device it means, “Keep your hands off.”
If you are asked to clean, clear out a jam or maintain machinery that exposes you to moving or energized parts, you must be trained in the machine-specific lockout procedure and follow that procedure exactly. In no case should you put your hands or body inside a machine that has not been properly locked out at the energy source by you.
PREVENTING SLIPS AND FALLS
You can reduce the risk of slipping by:
1. Taking your time and paying attention to where you are going 2. Adjusting your stride to a pace that is suitable for the walking surface and the task you are
doing 3. Walking with the feet pointing slightly outward 4. Making wide turns at corners 5. Wearing slip resistance shoes 6. Looking out for foreign substances on floors, such as: deposits of water, food, oil, sawdust,
soap, or debris 7. Immediately reporting, cleaning up and/or posting warnings about the presence of water
and other slipping hazards when you see them so others don’t slip.
You can reduce the risk of tripping by:
1. Keeping standing and walking areas clear from clutter or obstructions. Notify a site supervisor if necessary.
2. Keeping flooring in good condition 3. Always using installed light sources that provide sufficient light for your tasks 4. Using a flashlight if you enter a dark room where there is no light 5. Ensuring that things you are carrying or pushing do not prevent you from seeing any
obstructions, spills, etc.
21 Ladders and work at heights: WorkBox has height restrictions for temporary assignments. You should not climb ladders or work at heights that require your feet to be more than xx feet off the ground. 1. Inspect all ladders prior to each use 2. Ladders must be placed on secure footing 3. Only one person is allowed on a ladder at a time 4. Never stand on the top two steps of a stepladder 5. Always maintain 3-point contact when working on ladders 6. Never reach beyond arm length when working on a ladder 7. Never use metal ladders when working on or around electrical equipment or electrical
wires Other work at heights could include lifts or raised work areas. You must be trained by your site supervisor in proper fall protection guidelines and provided with adequate fall protection whenever you are working more than six feet off the ground. Cranes/Hoist/Lifting Devices: 1. Inspect all cranes, hoists, and lifting devices (slings, hooks, etc.) prior to each use, and
never use damaged equipment 2. Never walk under a load suspended from a hoist or crane 3. Keep all personnel clear of the ‘fall zone’ of the crane/hoist 4. Know the weight of material being lifted, and never overload a crane/hoist 5. Do not operate devices unless you have completed the required safety training
22 PROPER LIFTING TECHNIQUES
Plan ahead before lifting. Knowing what you're doing and where you're going will prevent you from making awkward movements while holding something heavy. Clear a path, and if lifting something with another person, make sure both of you agree on the plan.
Lift close to your body. You will be a stronger, and more stable lifter if the object is held close to your body rather than at the end of your reach. Make sure you have a firm hold on the object you are lifting, and keep it balanced close to your body.
Feet shoulder width apart. A solid base of support is important while lifting. Holding your feet too close together will be unstable, too far apart will hinder movement. Keep the feet about shoulder width apart and take short steps.
Bend your knees and keep your back straight. Practice the lifting motion before you lift the object, and think about your motion before you lift. Focus on keeping your spine straight--raise and lower to the ground by bending your knees.
Tighten your stomach muscles. Tightening your abdominal muscles will hold your back in a good lifting position and will help prevent excessive force on the spine.
Lift with your legs. Your legs are many times stronger than your back muscles--let your strength work in your favor. Again, lower to the ground by bending your knees, not your back. Keeping your eyes focused upwards helps to keep your back straight.
If you're straining, get help. If an object is too heavy, or awkward in shape, make sure you have someone around who can help you lift.
Wear a belt or back support. If you are lifting in your job or often at home, a back belt can help you maintain a better lifting posture.
TIPS
Never bend your back to pick something up. It's just not worth the damage that improper lifting technique can cause. Remember to use your leg muscles to help you lift properly.
Hold the object close to your body. You are a much more stable lifter if you're not reaching for an object.
Don't twist or bend. Face in the direction you are walking. If you need to turn, stop, turn in small steps, and then continue walking.
Keep your eyes up. Looking slightly upwards will help you maintain a better position of the spine.
